relevance_standard: Kept only cards a Class I-IV warrant board could plausibly ask a contracting officer (protest, claim, debriefing, termination, payment, options, publicizing, bonds, labor standards, subcontracting reports, property disposition the KO or TCO owns) or that teach a rule the KO applies personally; removed counts that only a specialist office applies, logged as 'removed: not board material'.

changes.source: RFO 4.203-1(c) is an exception for 4.203-1(b)(4) urgency awards only - https://www.acquisition.gov/far-overhaul/far-part-deviation-guide/far-overhaul-part-4

items.notes: 30 calendar days confirmed. RFO Part 2 makes an unqualified day a calendar day. Not a duplicate: PC65's 30 days is the FPDS report for urgency awards. Relevance: keep - a board can ask whether the awardee must be registered in SAM and the contracting officer validates the late registration. Difficulty lowered from 1 to 2: this is the urgency-award exception, not a headline deadline every contracting officer knows. Sources: https://www.acquisition.gov/far-overhaul/far-part-deviation-guide/far-overhaul-part-4 (4.203-1(b)(4), (c); 4.304(b)(1)) ; https://www.acquisition.gov/far/52.204-13 (paragraph (b))

changes.before: Table 5-3 sets the minimum time for receipt of quotations or offers. When an acquisition is subject to the WTO GPA or a free trade agreement but was not included in the agency's annual forecast, allow 40 days from the presolicitation notice or the solicitation, as applicable. The same 40 days applies to a commercial acquisition above the simplified acquisition threshold using a combined synopsis and solicitation, and to orders under a basic ordering agreement.
changes.after: Table 5-3 sets the minimum time for receipt of quotations or offers. For an acquisition from $15,000 up to the simplified acquisition threshold that is subject to the WTO GPA or a free trade agreement but was not included in the agency's annual forecast, allow 40 days from the presolicitation notice or the solicitation, as applicable. The same 40 days applies to a commercial acquisition above the threshold using a combined synopsis and solicitation and to orders under a basic ordering agreement; other noncommercial acquisitions above the threshold stay at 30 days from the solicitation.
changes.source: Table 5-3, third column, all five rows - https://www.acquisition.gov/far-overhaul/far-part-deviation-guide/far-overhaul-part-5

items.notes: 40 calendar days confirmed. The card's first sentence stated the 40 days as a general rule for any acquisition subject to a trade agreement and left out of the forecast, which over-applies it to noncommercial acquisitions above the SAT (30 days) and R&D (N/A); the rule now names the $15,000-to-SAT band and the 30-day row. Not a duplicate of PC72 (30 days) or PC73 (45 days). Relevance: keep (publicizing). Source: https://www.acquisition.gov/far-overhaul/far-part-deviation-guide/far-overhaul-part-5 (5.201(d), Table 5-3)

before.event: Contractor assertion that posted FAPIIS information is exempt from disclosure
before.anchor: after the information is posted to the non-public segment of FAPIIS
before.rule: Information covered by a Freedom of Information Act disclosure exemption must not be posted in the non-public segment of FAPIIS. If the contractor asserts within 7 calendar days, to the Government official who posted it, that some of the posted information is covered by a FOIA exemption, that official must remove the posting within 7 calendar days and resolve the issue under agency FOIA procedures before reposting anything releasable.
before.note: Read 17 Sep 2026: https://www.acquisition.gov/far-overhaul/far-part-deviation-guide/far-overhaul-part-9 (9.105-2(b)(2)(iv)). Both the contractor's assertion and the official's removal carry the same 7 calendar days.

items.notes: removed: not board material. Accurate as written: RFO 9.105-2(b)(2)(iv) gives the contractor 7 calendar days to assert a FOIA exemption to the official who posted the information, and that official 7 calendar days to remove it. But the actor is the posting official working agency FOIA procedures; a warrant board would not ask a Class I-IV contracting officer for this count (named as administrative minutiae in the review instruction). Source: https://www.acquisition.gov/far-overhaul/far-part-deviation-guide/far-overhaul-part-9 (9.105-2(b)(2)(iv))

before.event: Entering a debarment, suspension or other exclusion in SAM
before.rule: For each exclusion it takes, including a voluntary exclusion, the agency must enter the exclusion record information required by 9.404(b) into SAM within 3 business days after the action becomes effective.
before.note: Read 17 Sep 2026: https://www.acquisition.gov/far-overhaul/far-part-deviation-guide/far-overhaul-part-9 (9.404(c)(3)(i)). The exclusion record contents are listed at 9.404(b).

items.notes: removed: not board material. Accurate as written: RFO 9.404(c)(3)(i) requires each agency to enter the 9.404(b) exclusion record 'within 3 business days after the action becomes effective'. The duty belongs to the agency staff assigned SAM exclusion roles under 9.404(c)(1), not to the contracting officer, whose rule is to check SAM before award (9.404(c)(5), 9.405). Source: https://www.acquisition.gov/far-overhaul/far-part-deviation-guide/far-overhaul-part-9 (9.404(c)(1), (c)(3)(i))

before.event: Updating an exclusion record in SAM after the action is modified or rescinded
before.anchor: after modifying or rescinding an action
before.rule: The agency must update the exclusion record in SAM generally within 5 business days after modifying or rescinding an exclusion action.
before.note: Read 17 Sep 2026: https://www.acquisition.gov/far-overhaul/far-part-deviation-guide/far-overhaul-part-9 (9.404(c)(3)(iii)). The word 'generally' is in the source, so this is the standard rather than an absolute bar.

items.notes: removed: not board material. Accurate as written: RFO 9.404(c)(3)(iii) says 'Update the exclusion record in SAM, generally within 5 business days after modifying or rescinding an action'. Same specialist actor as PC85; named as administrative minutiae in the review instruction. Source: https://www.acquisition.gov/far-overhaul/far-part-deviation-guide/far-overhaul-part-9 (9.404(c)(3)(iii))

before.event: Notice to the prosecuting official before a suspension's 12-month period runs out
before.anchor: before the 12-month period after the suspension notice expires
before.rule: If legal proceedings are not initiated within 12 months after the date of the suspension notice, the suspension must be terminated unless a prosecuting official requests an extension, which can add 6 months; no suspension may run past 18 months without legal proceedings. The suspending and debarring official must notify the Department of Justice or other responsible prosecuting official of the proposed termination at least 30 days before the 12-month period expires, so that official can ask for an extension.
before.note: Read 17 Sep 2026: https://www.acquisition.gov/far-overhaul/far-part-deviation-guide/far-overhaul-part-9 (9.407-4(b) and (c)). The 12-month, 6-month and 18-month limits are stated in months, not days, so only the 30-day notice is scored here.

items.notes: removed: not board material. Accurate as written: RFO 9.407-4(b) (12 months, extension of 6 months on a prosecuting official's request, never beyond 18 months without legal proceedings) and 9.407-4(c) (the suspending and debarring official notifies DOJ or the responsible prosecuting official 'at least 30 days before the 12-month period expires'). The board-askable part is the 12/6/18-month suspension length, which is stated in months and cannot be scored; the 30 days that the card scores is the suspending and debarring official's notice to a prosecutor, which only that office applies. Source: https://www.acquisition.gov/far-overhaul/far-part-deviation-guide/far-overhaul-part-9 (9.407-4(b)-(c))

before.event: Award of a multiyear contract after congressional notification
before.anchor: after the agency head notifies Congress in writing
before.rule: Except for DoD, NASA and the Coast Guard, a multiyear contract with a cancellation ceiling over $20 million may not be awarded until the agency head notifies Congress in writing; for DoD, NASA and the Coast Guard the trigger is a ceiling over $200 million and the notice goes to the House and Senate armed services and appropriations committees. The contract may not be awarded until 31 days after notification.
before.note: Read 17 Sep 2026: https://www.acquisition.gov/far-overhaul/far-part-deviation-guide/far-overhaul-part-17 (17.104-3 Congressional notification, paragraphs (a), (b) and (c)).

items.notes: removed: not board material. Accurate as written: RFO 17.104-3(a)-(c) - cancellation ceiling over $20 million (civilian) or $200 million (DoD, NASA, Coast Guard), agency-head notice to Congress or the armed services and appropriations committees, and 'The contract may not be awarded until 31 days after notification.' A multiyear contract with a cancellation ceiling over $200 million is outside anything a Class I-IV contracting officer at a contracting support brigade would award, and a board question on Part 17 goes to options and the multiyear versus multiple-year distinction, not this count. Source: https://www.acquisition.gov/far-overhaul/far-part-deviation-guide/far-overhaul-part-17 (17.104-3)

before.event: Standard screening period for reutilization of contractor inventory
before.anchor: from the plant clearance officer's acceptance of an inventory disposal schedule
before.rule: The screening period begins when the plant clearance officer accepts an inventory disposal schedule. The standard screening period is 46 days: the contracting agency screens during the first 20 days, days 21 through 41 are concurrent screening by other Federal agencies and screening for donation, and days 42 through 46 are reserved for GSA to allocate property to donees.

findings.sources_read: Every card checked against the live text fetched 17 Sep 2026 from acquisition.gov (RFO deviation-guide pages for Parts 4, 5, 9, 14, 17, 19, 22, 28, 32, 42, 45 and 49, all marked Last Updated 09/14/2026; clause pages 52.204-13, 52.219-9, 52.222-41, 52.228-1, 52.232-20, 52.232-25, 52.242-14, 52.245-1, FAC 2026-01). author_report: PC88: the author's note '31 days, not 30' is correct (RFO 17.104-3(c)); the card was removed for relevance, not accuracy.
PC92: the author read the clause correctly (dates and a 30-day due date) but cited the prescription as RFO 19.109(a)(2)(i); the clause is prescribed at 19.109(e)(2)(i). Fixed.

PC111: I agree with both of the author's observations - the candidate list's '20 days after the suspension ends' is not in 52.242-14, and RFO 42.1005(a)'s sentence about reducing 'the 90-day period in the clause' is a drafting slip that belongs with 52.242-15.
PC81: the author's note that it is distinct from PC64 is right, but the anchor added 'before the solicitation is issued', which Table 5-2 does not say for the 10-day row. Fixed.
PC82: the author's note correctly lists the rows carrying 40 days; the rule's first sentence stated the 40 days more broadly than the table. Fixed.
PC78: RFO 4.203-1(b)(4) reads 'unusual or compelling urgency'; the card says 'unusual and compelling urgency' (the Part 6 authority's name). Left as written.
